chapter: Postwar Poland and jazz under Stalinism
title: Jazz banned as decadent Western music, 1948-52
summary: Until Stalin's death, jazz was officially discouraged and survived only privately.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Do you have it here? Mm-hmm. You talked there about decadent capitalism, the capitalists of the UK. Yes, yes, something like that, it's called so. Decadent music and so on.

It was, of course, the same language like in Russia, because they didn't believe that it is also art, yes. And they told that all music that came from America, it is not a good music, so we can listen only Polish music, Russian music, and of course, our old composers from symphonic music and so on. That is the reason that it comes time for listening jazz only at home, on private meetings, in schools, and dancing, private dancing and so on. Non-official life of jazz. Mm-hm.
